Particularly, this section will focus on AI’s functionality beyond the domain of training data by enabling better generalizability, uncertainty quantification, explainability, or reasoning capability. These capabilities allow AI to contribute to design innovation in two key ways: synthesizing creative solutions and extracting useful insights to foster creativity. Note that our scope is not limited to data-driven approaches. 

Potential topics include, but are not limited to
•	The effectiveness or limitations of generative AI (e.g., deep generative models, large language models, and agentic AI systems) in design innovation
•	Trustworthy and explainable AI methods that support design innovation
•	Generative design methodologies that promote creativity
•	AI techniques for novel bio-inspired design discovery
•	Symbolic reasoning and knowledge graphs for identifying design rules or governing mechanisms
•	AI-driven tools that stimulate new design ideas
•	Metrics and Methods to characterize and measure novelty and creativity in AI-generated designs
•	AI/ML-based inverse design methods that are effective with sparse data and can generalize to a wider range of scenarios
•	Reinforcement learning or evolutionary computation methods that can generate novel design solutions
•	Methods to extract generalizable design principles 
•	Studies on how human-AI collaboration can promote creativity

Topic Name: DAC-21: Early Career Research: Lightning Talks
Topic Description: This special symposium aims to provide early career researchers, including junior scientists, research faculty, post-doctoral fellows, and junior assistant professors, a robust platform to present exciting Late Breaking Results. To be eligible for this symposium, the presenter must be within five years of receiving their Doctoral Degree. With this goal, we invite early career researchers to submit a presentation-only abstract that leads to a 15-minute talk highlighting exciting developments in their research. All Design Automation topics, as covered by the other sessions under DAC, are within the scope of this special symposium.

Topic Name: DAC-22: Cultivating Datasets for Engineering Design
Topic Description:
In today's rapidly evolving world, data has become crucial across industries, especially in engineering. Tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Stable Diffusion have been enabled mostly by extensive and well-accessible datasets, and have shown to the greater public the capabilities of data-driven methods. In engineering design, data-driven methodologies have also contributed to advances in design theory, decision processes, optimization techniques, and educational programs. In particular, these approaches also enable faster design exploration and real-time operational management. However, implementing machine learning in engineering design faces several obstacles: a scarcity of publicly accessible datasets, insufficient sample sizes and feature counts in existing datasets, and a lack of high-quality datasets that incorporate functional performance metrics.
The IDETC session on datasets would provide a platform for the design community to discuss what is high-quality data, publicly release datasets, and present methods for sampling, collecting, cleaning, and using data, to specifically address the needs of engineering designs. Some critical challenges in engineering dataset creation include multi-modality, user inputs, handling missing information, managing diverse data types, navigating dependencies among attributes, ensuring data quality, and integrating complex data structures and real-time data.
To differentiate from other data-driven sessions, submissions to this session need to release a novel dataset as part of their submission and dedicate a section of their paper to describing the dataset and its relevance for engineering design.

Topic Name: DAC-23: Digital Twin for Design and Decision-making
Topic Description:
Digital twin technology, often regarded as one of the most transformative developments in recent years, is reshaping both scientific discovery and industrial practices. By establishing a dynamic, bidirectional connection between physical systems and their virtual counterparts, digital twins offer a real-time, continuously updated model that evolves with its real-world counterpart. Unlike traditional modeling and simulation, digital twins allow for predictive capabilities that extend beyond existing data, offering critical insights to inform both automated and human decision-making processes.
This session, organized by the ASME Design Automation Committee, serves as a premier platform for researchers, engineers, and industry professionals to share state-of-the-art developments in digital twin technology with applications for design automation and decision-making. We invite submissions that introduce innovative techniques, groundbreaking methodologies, and novel research directions in the development and application of digital twins. 

Topics may include, but are not limited to:
Topic 1: Digital Twin Fundamentals
•	Concepts and theories
•	Architecture and frameworks
•	Methodology, lifecycle, and processes
•	Data-driven modeling and technologies
•	Validation, verification, and uncertainty quantification
Topic 2: Digital Twin Interaction and Communication, Security, and Privacy
•	Interaction between physical and virtual twins
•	Distributed digital twin systems
•	User interactions with digital twins
•	Digital twins for cybersecurity
Topic 3: Digital Twin Systems and Applications
•	Automation and manufacturing
•	Digital health and assisted systems
•	Smart cities and transportation
•	Automotive and aerospace
•	Sustainable energy

Topic Name: DAC-24: Design for E-Mobility
Topic Description:
The rapid growth of electric mobility—including electric vehicles, aircraft, and marine systems—requires breakthroughs in material design, battery innovation, structural optimization, and energy harvesting technologies. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers powerful tools for accelerating these advances by enabling data-driven modeling, generative design, and multi-scale optimization across materials, devices, and systems. This symposium will highlight the integration of AI into the design of next-generation e-mobility technologies, with emphasis on energy-efficient, sustainable, and high-performance solutions.

Topics of interest include:
•	AI-guided design automation for multifunctional components in electrified mobility platforms
•	Data-driven modelling and optimization of battery and hybrid energy storage systems for transportation
•	Design of structural systems for electric ground vehicles, urban air mobility, and marine platforms
•	AI-enabled design for on-board energy harvesting and management in mobile systems
•	Generative design and topology optimization targeting multifunctional e-mobility components
•	Digital twins for real-time monitoring and predictive design of batteries, materials, and subsystems in mobility
•	Lifecycle-aware design strategies for sustainable and circular e-mobility solutions
•	System-level integration of propulsion, storage, and renewable charging infrastructures for mobility
•	Application-driven case studies in electrified transportation ecosystems
•	Quantum and high-performance computing for next-generation design automation in mobility systems

Topic Name: DFMLC-01: Circular Economy Design and Impact Assessment
Topic Description:
The ASME DFMLC Committee and the organizers of the session on Circular Economy Design and Impact Assessment invite full papers, reviews, and technical presentations in the areas of circular product design, circular supply chains, and measuring circularity impacts. Submissions may deal with modeling, methodology, cost estimation, standards and tools, case studies, and industrial applications.

Concerns about overconsumption, overproduction, and waste generation have led to public policy and company commitments that pose a transition to a circular economy to alleviate these concerns. To ensure the successful implementation of circularity, new methods of measurement are needed to predict, characterize, and improve the environmental, economic, and social performance of existing and future product systems. The topics of this session will consider, but are not limited to, the following subjects: performance-driven circular product design, defining circularity for emerging industries, circularity assessment and measurement, social impact consideration for circularity, and supply chain coordination to support circularity. This year, we ask all authors to discuss knowledge or technology transfer across applications, domains, and geographies, as well as the scalability, both up and down, of solutions presented in their work.

Topic Name: DFMLC-02: Decision Making in Life Cycle and Human Factors Design
Topic Description: The ASME DFMLC Committee and the organizers of the session on Life Cycle and Human Factors Decision Making invite full papers, reviews, and technical presentations on decision making in product life cycle management and service life cycles. Submissions may deal with domain modeling, methodology, standards and tools, case studies, and industrial applications. Typically, life cycle and human factor decisions are made under uncertainty, have great influences on the outcome, and often need to take into account the trade-offs involving different parameters, conflicting and changing requirements, and multiple stakeholders. Submissions related to visualization and communication during design and decision making are of particular interest. This year we ask all authors to discuss knowledge or technology transfer across applications, domains, and geographies as well as scalability, both up and down, of solutions presented in their work.

Topic Name: DFMLC-04: Design for Large and Distributed Systems

Topic Name: DFMLC-05: Design for Manufacturing, Assembly, and Integration
Topic Description: The ASME DFMLC Committee and the organizers of the session on Design for Manufacturing, Assembly, and Integration invite full papers, reviews, and technical presentations covering design principles for minimizing the number of parts, ease of fabrication, ease of assembly, ease of packaging, modular design, tolerance analysis, geometric dimensioning tolerancing (GD&T), and optimization of manufacturing and assembly processes. Topic Name: DFMLC-06: Design for Recycling and End-of-Life
Topic Description: The ASME DFMLC Committee and the Organizers of the session on Design for Recycling and End-of-Life invite full papers, reviews, and technical presentations related to recycling and end-of-life considerations. Topics of interest include but are not limited to design for recycling and recovery of high-value materials, battery recycling, system decomissioning and reuse, system life and cost predictions considering retirement, used part re-validation and certification, recycling standards, use of recycled materials and parts in space, testing standards, part functionality degredation, and related areas. Topic Name: DFMLC-07: Design for Remanufacturing and Multiple Life Cycles

Areas of interest include remanufacturing and refurbishment of consumer products, redesign of legacy parts and systems for new manufacturing processes, recovery, cleaning, and reassembly processes, design of products and systems for remanufacturing, design of products for multiple life cycles, evaluation methods, modeling, cost and life cycle analysis related to remanufacturing, certification and re-certification processes, risk analysis, and related topics. Topic Name: DFMLC-08: Design for Supply Chain and Mass Customization
Topic Description: The ASME DFMLC Committee and the organizers of the session on Design for Supply Chain, Circular Economy, and Mass Customization invite full papers, reviews, and technical presentations in areas of the product supply chain, inventory management, mass customization, product disassembly, re-use, design for take-back management, design for upgrade, performance analysis of recovery operations, end-of-life (EOL) profitability, circular economy, market positioning and consumer preference modeling of used products, and related topics. Topic Name: DFMLC-09: Design of Product-Service and Energy Systems
Topic Description: The ASME DFMLC Committee and the organizers of the session on Design for Product-Service and Energy Systems invite full papers, reviews, and technical presentations in the areas of product mass customization and product-service systems. Submissions may deal with domain modeling, methodology, cost estimating of PSS, standards and tools, case studies, and industrial applications. Concerns over sustainable production and consumption have led to the transformation of market structures and competitive situations into the direction of customization, flexibility, and servitization, i.e. competing through services as opposed to competing through products. The topics of this session will consider but are not limited to the following subjects: Green buildings, energy-efficient industrial systems, renewable energy systems, electric power systems, life cycle in energy manufacturing systems, and power for transportation systems (aircrafts, automobiles, ships, trains). Topic Name: DFMLC-10/DAC-11: Joint Session Engineering for Sustainable Development (ESD)
Topic Description:
Engineering for Sustainable Development (ESD) refers to the broad interdisciplinary practice of engineering to improve the quality of life of society and the environment worldwide. Our world faces challenges of unprecedented scale, such as climate change, food insecurity, disease, access to safe and reliable water, and growing economic inequality. Making progress towards solving such challenges requires interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary approaches from various backgrounds and fields. Engineers can play pivotal roles in addressing these challenges by reducing the progression of climate change, mitigating the impact of global and local emergencies, promoting economic development, reducing inequality, and advancing social justice and sustainable development. 

In particular, the DFMLC and DAC technical committees have initiated a joint session on “Design for the Sustainable Development Goals across the Life Cycle” and invite full papers, reviews, and technical presentations related to design for one or more of the seventeen United Nations 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) - across product, system, and/or service life cycles. Areas of interest include material processing, energy production, manufacturing, material recycling, remanufacturing, impact analysis, modeling, and related topics. Projects related to climate change, clean water and sanitation, clean energy, resilient infrastructure, sustainable cities, and sustainable consumption and production are of particular interest. This year we ask all authors to discuss knowledge or technology transfer across applications, domains, and geographies as well as scalability, both up and down, of solutions presented in their work.

Topic Name: DFMLC-11/DAC-17: Joint Session Modeling and Optimization for Sustainable Design and Manufacturing
Topic Description: The ASME DFMLC Committee and the organizers of the session on Modeling and Optimization for Sustainable Design and Manufacturing invite full papers, reviews, and technical presentations that deal with all topics relevant to sustainable design, sustainable manufacturing, and decision-support tools. This session focuses on the balance of the “triple-bottom-line” of social, environmental, and economic issues affecting a system throughout its lifecycle. It includes topics such as integrating sustainability into conceptual design, computer-enabled methods and tools to influence sustainable design, design for environmentally conscious manufacturing, design for remanufacturing and reuse, ecological design, decision-support tools for sustainability, incorporation of social decision factors, consumer preference modeling for sustainability, and use of novel materials and devices to create sustainable manufacturing processes. Submitted papers may deal with domain modeling, methodology, tools, metrics and indices, case studies, and industrial applications. Design and visualization tools, automated methods, and case studies are of particular interest. This year, we ask all authors to discuss knowledge or technology transfer across applications, domains, and geographies as well as scalability, both up and down, of solutions presented in their work.

Topic Name: DTM-01: Benchmarking Design Research Progress
Topic Description: How do we measure progress in Design Research? What makes a design benchmark good or better compared to others? What would be a set of necessary or sufficient benchmarks needed to measure progress in design, and what is the field missing? What kind of research, technological, or social infrastructure do we need to develop as a community to enable better use, development, discovery, and prioritization of benchmarks? Do we encourage benchmarks that have broad industry applicability/relevance or that are approachable by researchers, or both, and what is needed to drive adoption? This session invites papers that address not just new benchmark or dataset development but also (1) comparative analysis of existing/recent benchmarks that propose gaps in our current portfolio, (2) studies of existing metrics or benchmarks that show how our existing benchmarks are not used properly or do not account for important/relevant design factors, (3) technological advances that enable better benchmarking across Design problems, (4) industry perspectives on why existing benchmarks or datasets produced by our community are missing critical elements, or even (5) papers that criticize the epistemological assumptions of using benchmarks to study design research progress.

Topic Name: DTM-02: Design Theory and Methodology in Practice and Industry
Topic Description: This session explores current gaps and needs in design practice and industry, or reports on recent successes or failures in the application of emerging theories or methods in practice. Specifically, papers could include, but are not limited to, topics such as (1) analysis of existing gaps or needs within industry or practice that current research does not sufficiently address, (2) observed differences between laboratory and industrial environments or theory application, (3) critical empirical assessments of method application within a practical context, and (4) industry-driven discussions about necessary technologies, roadmaps, or problems for which advances in Design Theory and Methodology could be well equipped to solve.

Topic Name: DTM-03: Designer & Team Thinking and Behavior
Topic Description: This topic solicits papers addressing mathematical, computational, or empirical work that builds or tests models of human thinking or behavior, whether in teams or as individuals. Such papers could include (but are not limited to) submissions on (1) experiments of designer behavior (e.g., protocol studies, randomized control trials), (2) analysis or interventions for modifying the cognitive state or ability of designers or design teams (including work on team management, creativity, work product, etc.), (3) testable models of human performance in the context of design activities, or (4) computational/mathematical theories or surrogates of human behavior relevant to a design context.

Topic Name: DTM-04: Human-AI Design Collaboration
Topic Description: This session covers the growing intersection of Human-AI collaboration in the design process. This could include, but is not limited to, papers covering topics such as (1) proposed interaction models or approaches that can improve Human-AI interaction experience in a design context, (2) empirical studies of humans in the design process (whether they are designers or stakeholders) and how they currently interact with AI tools, or (3) theoretical, computational, or mathematical models that describe Human-AI interaction behavior or outcomes.

Topic Name: DTM-05: New Mathematical or Computational Models of Design
Topic Description: This session focuses on new or updated mathematical or computational models of design, whether those be of designed artifacts themselves, of the design process, or of individual agents/actors doing design tasks. For example, submitted papers could include, but are not limited to, topics such as: (1) new mathematical representations of Function, Behaviors, or Structures with designed artifacts, (2) novel mathematical or computational representations of design processes, (3) predictive and testable models of agent behavior (human, AI, or hybrid) within a design context, and (4) multi- or cross-modal representations of design that enable more predictive and accurate theories of design from within or across lifecycle stages.

Topic Name: DTM-06: Rethinking Design in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
Topic Description: Our current theories about, models of, and methods for design are largely based on how humans have historically practiced design or on human-centric theories about how design ought to be performed. Yet, rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence capabilities have fundamentally transformed how other fields approach discovery and innovation, whether that be in Software Engineering, new Material chemistries, Synthetic biology and protein engineering, Automated Theorem Proving, among many others. How should Engineering Design change and adapt to a possible future where AI is not just an active partner/collaborator with humans, but potentially even a leading agent? Do existing design processes that we currently teach and use -- such as the typical product development stages, iterative variants of them, user-centered approaches like Design Thinking, or classical Systems Engineering paradigms -- that were designed for humans, still make sense in a world where possibly tens or hundreds of agents can explore and refine millions of options or designs in parallel? This session invites papers that rethink, fundamentally transform, or debate our underlying design theories, methods, processes, and practices in a world where AI is not just collaborating, but potentially a driving decision-making force within the design process. Submitted paper topics can include, but are not limited to, (1) computational models of design processes that heavily leverage AI as a first-class citizen and comparisons to existing human-crafted design processes, (2) proposed metrics for measuring and evaluating AI-generated design processes or artifacts that differ significantly from established metrics, or (3) empirical studies of modifications to practice or teaching of design processes that leverage AI-driven approaches.

Topic Name: DTM-07: Social, Justice, and Ethical Impacts within Design
Topic Description: This session invites papers addressing how Design Theory and Methodology research intersects and impacts social, ethical, or justice related topics. Submitted papers can include, but are not limited to, topics such as (1) empirical analysis of existing data on impacts and what this implies for existing practice or research, (2) effective interventions, or proposed theories or testable models, that could predict or modify existing impacts, (3) novel frameworks or lenses that modify our understanding of existing impacts, or (4) metrics, testbeds, benchmarks, or datasets that could improve our ability to understand a broader range of design impacts than is presently easy to assess.

Topic Name: DTM-08: Theory Development in Design Research
Topic Description: This session advances the development of theory in design research. Design “theory” is in DTM’s name, but the degree to which we build theory, or reflect on theory development, is relatively low compared to other fields, which has implications for the practical and scientific impacts of design research. Here, we understand theory development broadly, building from initial results, through frameworks and conceptual models toward more fully realised theory. We are soliciting both full-length and abstract-only papers with suggested topics that include: understandings of theory and theory development, approaches to developing theory, reflections on adaption or elaboration of theory from other fields, considerations for theory-methodology fit, methodological guidance for building or testing theory using qualitative work, simulations, experiments, etc., and characterizations of the use of theory in design research.

Topic Name: MNS-01: Dynamics and Control of Micro/Nano Systems
Topic Description:
This symposium highlights recent advances in the dynamics, modeling, analysis, and control of micro- and nano-scale systems, with a focus on nonlinear phenomena, multiphysics interactions, and emerging applications. It aims to provide a forum for researchers from experimental, theoretical, and computational backgrounds to exchange ideas and foster collaborations in this rapidly evolving field.

Micro- and nano-systems such as MEMS and NEMS often exhibit complex dynamics driven by coupled physical domains, nonlinearities, and collective behaviors. Understanding and controlling these phenomena is critical for enabling next-generation technologies in sensing, actuation, energy systems, and biomedical devices. The symposium “Dynamics and Control of Micro/Nano Systems” will cover, but not be limited to, the following topics:

- Dynamics and vibration behavior of MEMS and NEMS
- Control and modeling of multi-body micro- and nano-systems
- Stability, robustness, and feedback control of micro/nano systems
- Dynamics and control of coupled thermal, electrostatic, magnetic, and elastic MEMS/NEMS
- Collective behaviors in MEMS/NEMS, such as localization and synchronization
- Nonlinear dynamics and bifurcations in MEMS/NEMS
- System identification, reduced-order modeling, and computational methods for dynamics and control
- Innovative approaches to sensing and actuation based on nonlinear MEMS/NEMS
- Adaptive, reconfigurable, and self-tuning micro/nano systems
- Data-driven, machine learning, and intelligent control methods for MEMS/NEMS

Topic Name: MNS-02: Micro/Nano Bioengineering and Fluidics
Topic Description:
This symposium highlights cutting-edge research at the intersection of micro/nano-scale engineering, fluid dynamics, and biological systems. With the rapid development of micro- and nano-technologies, new opportunities have emerged for advancing healthcare, biotechnology, and life sciences through novel diagnostic, therapeutic, and analytical platforms.

Topics of interest span across microfluidics, nanofluidics, and bio-MEMS/NEMS, with particular emphasis on lab-on-a-chip devices, organ-on-chip models, biosensing platforms, and biomedical applications of micro- and nano-engineering. Contributions that integrate design, fabrication, experimental validation, and computational modeling are especially encouraged, as they enable transformative solutions to critical challenges in biology, medicine, and biotechnology. The symposium “Micro/Nano Bioengineering and Fluidics” will cover, but not be limited to, the following topics: 

- Microfluidics and nanofluidics: transport phenomena, mixing, separation, and manipulation of fluids at small scales
- Lab-on-a-chip and organ-on-chip platforms for diagnostics, drug discovery, and personalized medicine
- MEMS/NEMS for biomedical applications, including implantable and wearable devices
- Biosensors and bioactuators at the micro/nano scale
- Micro/nano-scale manipulation of cells, biomolecules, and extracellular vesicles
- Single-cell analysis, point-of-care testing, and minimally invasive diagnostics
- Micro/nano-engineered platforms for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and organ modeling
- Interaction of biological systems with micro/nano materials, surfaces, and structures
- Micro/nano-scale fluid–structure interactions and soft matter systems
- Computational modeling and simulation of bio-micro/nanofluidic systems
- Emerging materials and fabrication techniques for bio-micro/nano devices
- Integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data analytics with bio-micro/nano systems

Topic Name: MNS-03: Micro/Nano Robotics
Topic Description:
This symposium explores the rapidly growing field of micro- and nano-robotics, focusing on advances in design, fabrication, modeling, control, and applications of robotic systems operating at extremely small scales. Micro/nano-robots are emerging as powerful tools for manipulation, sensing, and actuation in environments inaccessible to conventional robots, with broad impact in biomedical, industrial, and environmental domains.

Special emphasis will be placed on bio-inspired and soft robotics, swarm and collective behaviors, autonomous systems, and strategies for microrobotic manipulation. Contributions that combine novel materials, innovative fabrication processes, intelligent control, and cross-disciplinary applications are particularly encouraged. The symposium “Micro/Nano Robotics” will cover, but not be limited to, the following topics:

- Design, fabrication, and integration of micro/nano robotic systems
- Actuation mechanisms at the micro/nano scale (magnetic, acoustic, optical, chemical, electrostatic, etc.)
- Modeling, dynamics, and control of micro/nano robots
- Bio-inspired and soft micro/nano robotic systems
- Swarm robotics and collective behaviors of micro/nano robots
- Autonomous navigation, sensing, and decision-making at small scales
- Microrobotic manipulation of cells, biomolecules, and microscale structures
- Applications in targeted drug delivery, minimally invasive surgery, and precision medicine
- Micro/nano robots for environmental monitoring, inspection, and remediation
- Advanced imaging, localization, and tracking techniques for micro/nano robotic systems
- Emerging materials and fabrication methods for micro/nano robotics
- Machine learning, AI, and data-driven control for intelligent micro/nano robotic systems
- Hybrid platforms integrating micro/nano robots with MEMS, NEMS, and bio-microfluidic devices

Topic Name: MNS-04: Micro/Nano Materials and Manufacturing
Topic Description:
This symposium focuses on advances in materials, fabrication methods, and manufacturing technologies for MEMS, NEMS, and other micro/nano-scale devices. It aims to highlight innovative approaches that enhance the performance, functionality, and scalability of small-scale systems through novel materials, advanced processing techniques, and integrated manufacturing strategies. Contributions that combine experimental, computational, and theoretical approaches to solve critical challenges in micro/nano materials and manufacturing are particularly encouraged. The symposium “Micro/Nano Materials and Manufacturing” will cover, but not be limited to, the following topics:

- Advanced micro- and nano-scale materials, including functional, composite, and hybrid materials
- Additive manufacturing techniques for MEMS/NEMS (3D printing, micro-stereolithography, etc.)
- Subtractive manufacturing and precision micromachining methods
- Surface engineering, coatings, and functionalization strategies for micro/nano devices
- Micro/nano-scale assembly and integration techniques
- Scalable fabrication methods for high-throughput production
- Materials and processes for flexible, stretchable, and soft micro/nano devices
- Process optimization and reliability assessment of micro/nano manufacturing
- Lithography, etching, and deposition methods for MEMS/NEMS fabrication
- Multiphysics simulation and modeling for process design and optimization
- Hybrid fabrication approaches combining top-down and bottom-up methods
- Integration strategies for complex micro/nano systems and multi-functional devices
- Characterization techniques for material properties, structural integrity, and device performance

Topic Name: MNS-05: Micro/Nano IoT, Sensors, and Computing
Topic Description:
This symposium focuses on recent advances in micro- and nano-scale sensing, data acquisition, processing, and computing systems for Internet of Things (IoT) and smart system applications. It aims to highlight innovations that enhance the performance, efficiency, reliability, and scalability of micro/nano systems for sensing, communication, and embedded computation. Contributions that integrate novel device design, low-power electronics, advanced data acquisition, and intelligent system architectures are particularly encouraged. The symposium “Micro/Nano IoT, Sensors, and Computing” will cover, but not be limited to, the following topics:

- Design and fabrication of micro/nano sensors for physical, chemical, and biological sensing
- Low-power electronics and energy-efficient circuits for IoT applications
- Embedded computing, microcontrollers, and real-time processing at the micro/nano scale
- Wireless communication and networking strategies for micro/nano IoT systems
- Smart system integration, including sensor fusion, actuation, and feedback control
- Data acquisition, signal processing, and machine learning for micro/nano systems
- Edge and cloud computing solutions for micro/nano IoT devices
- Security, privacy, and reliability of micro/nano-scale IoT networks
- Energy harvesting and self-powered micro/nano sensors
- MEMS/NEMS-enabled sensors and devices for real-world IoT applications
- System-level design, optimization, and deployment strategies
- Cross-disciplinary applications in environmental monitoring, healthcare, industrial automation, and smart cities

Topic Name: MR-01: Mechanism Synthesis and Analysis
Topic Description: This track focuses on the design, modeling, and performance evaluation of mechanical linkages and robotic architectures. Topics include dimensional synthesis, type synthesis, mobility analysis, motion generation, and optimization of mechanisms for innovative applications. Contributions that advance creative design methods including AI-based methods or reveal new insights into classical mechanism behavior are particularly welcome.

Topic Name: MR-02: Theoretical and Computational Kinematics (A. T. Yang Symposium)
Topic Description: This track addresses fundamental advances in kinematic theory, computation, and geometry for mechanisms and robotic systems. Topics include configuration spaces, singularity analysis, motion interpolation, screw theory, algebraic and numerical methods for displacement analysis, and computational algorithms for spatial kinematics. Papers emphasizing mathematical rigor and theoretical innovation are encouraged.

Topic Name: MR-03: Compliant Mechanisms (A. Midha Symposium)
Topic Description: Papers are solicited in all areas of compliant mechanism design and analysis. Topics include design, modeling, and optimization of compliant systems for precision engineering, energy harvesting, deployable structures, bio-inspired devices and other applications. Both analytical and experimental studies demonstrating innovative compliant behavior or fabrication techniques are welcome.

Topic Name: MR-04: Origami-Based Engineering Design
Topic Description: This track focuses on the analysis, design, and application of origami and folding-inspired structures and mechanisms. Topics include fold pattern design, rigid and non-rigid origami mechanics, deployable systems, morphing structures, and novel manufacturing approaches. Papers that bridge geometry, materials, and mechanical functionality are particularly encouraged.

Topic Name: MR-05: Motion Planning, Dynamics, and Control of Robots
Topic Description:
Papers are solicited in the areas of motion planning, dynamics, and control of robots and mechanisms. Theoretical, experimental, and computational aspects are all invited. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:
●	Legged and mobile robots
●	Serial and parallel robots
●	Cable robot and tensegrity mechanism
●	Dynamic analysis, modeling, and simulation
●	Control methods and controller design
●	Trajectory optimization and optimal control
●	Applications of machine learning and AI
●	Manipulation and locomotion planning
●	Stability and efficiency
●	Mission planning, path planning, and motion planning for robots and autonomous systems

Topic Name: MR-06: Medical and Rehabilitation Robotics
Topic Description: This track highlights robotic and mechatronic systems designed for medical, surgical, assistive, and rehabilitative applications. Topics include device design, human–robot interaction, control, sensing, and clinical validation. Submissions emphasizing patient-centered design, safety, and novel approaches to physical human–robot collaboration are especially welcome.

Topic Name: MR-07: Novel Mechanisms, Robots, and Applications
Topic Description: This track invites papers presenting innovative mechanisms and robot designs that extend the boundaries of current applications. Topics include unconventional actuation and transmission systems, reconfigurable and modular robots, bio-inspired designs, and emerging applications in manufacturing, construction, agriculture, and exploration. Emphasis is placed on creativity, functionality, and demonstrated utility.

Topic Name: MR-08: Soft and Continuous Mechanisms
Topic Description: This track focuses on the design, modeling, and control of mechanisms and robots with distributed compliance, continuum structures, or soft materials. Topics include modeling of continuum kinematics and dynamics, material-based actuation, sensing and control strategies, and novel fabrication techniques. Papers that advance the understanding or practical deployment of soft robotic systems are encouraged.

Topic Name: MR-09: MR/MESA Joint Symposium on Translation Robotics
Topic Description: This symposium focuses on use-inspired translational research that brings advances in robotics research to the practicing engineer by emphasizing creative solutions to real-world problems and sharing innovations in implementation details. It is expected that the research results are demonstrated with a minimally viable prototype or an experimental verification. The papers submitted to this symposium will have the option to be considered for publication in ASME Letters in Translational Robotics

Topic Name: MSNDC-01 Nonlinear Dynamics and Control of Smart Structures and Systems
Topic Description:
The Symposium is focused on Nonlinear Dynamics and Control of Smart Structures and Systems across different scales, from the nano- to the meso-scale, including nanocomposites and metamaterials-based structures, MEMS and NEMS, and the macro-scale, including complex mechanical systems. The relevant systems involve innovative applications in the field of mechanical engineering. The symposium gathers researchers from industry, academia, and government agencies working in the most innovative areas of nonlinear dynamics and vibration to discuss recent developments in experimental, analytical, and numerical techniques as applied to the synthesis, characterization, and control of Smart Materials and Structures, and Complex Systems. Papers are welcome in the area of analytical modeling and numerical simulations of linear and nonlinear dynamic phenomena, numerical and analytical studies on the dynamic stability of systems, wave propagation and absorption, vibration control and experimental characterization of nonlinear dynamic behaviors. The symposium also intends to encourage interactions between theoretical and applied researchers working in the most innovative areas of nonlinear dynamics. The symposium will also be a great opportunity for disseminating recent developments of experimental, analytical and numerical techniques, and for discussing novel phenomena and behaviors characterizing smart materials and structures. The symposium “Nonlinear Dynamics and Control of Smart Structures and Systems” will cover, but will not be limited to, the following topics:
This symposium will cover, but will not be limited to, the following topics:
    • characterization of the vibration and dynamic response of smart structures and systems.
    • reduced-order modeling of smart structures and systems.
    • nonlinear dynamics of continuous and discontinuous mechanical systems.
    • nonlinear dynamic phenomena and interactions in mechanical systems and structures.
    • dynamic stability of nonlinear systems due to multiphysics interaction.
    • experimental studies of observed linear and nonlinear dynamic phenomena.
    • wave propagation and absorption in smart structures and systems.
    • bifurcations and chaos in dynamic systems.
    • asymptotic methods in nonlinear dynamics.
    • non-smooth systems.
    • novel vibration control devices.
    • hybrid techniques that blend active and passive vibration control.
    • dynamics and vibrations of MEMS and NEMS
    • dynamics and control of multi-body micro- and nano-systems
    • dynamics and control of coupled thermal, electrostatic, magnetic, elastic MEMS/NEMS.
    • collective behaviors, such as localization and synchronization in MEMS/ NEMS
    • innovative concepts of sensing and actuating based on nonlinear MEMS/ NEMS.

Topic Name: MSNDC-02 Nonlinear Dynamics of Systems and Nonlinear Phenomena
Topic Description:
Real-world problems seldom adhere to linear or nearly linear behaviors. Decades of work has led to the explorations of a galaxy of nonlinear dynamics phenomena, unveiling terrains for exciting applications across the spectrum of science and engineering. Today, we stand witness to the flourishing of significant and exciting new advances in nonlinear dynamics far beyond the known limitations. This forthcoming joint symposium is designed to serve as a forum for exchanging insights and discussions on recent breakthroughs in theoretical, computational, experimental, and applied aspects of modeling, analyzing, and controlling nonlinear systems. Papers in the following areas are particularly encouraged:

    • Nonlinear Resonances, Phenomena, and Interactions  
    • Dynamic Systems with Time-Variability, Delay, or Discontinuities  
    • Reduced-Order Modelling  
    • Fractional Dynamics  
    • Structural Dynamics  
    • Flexible Slender Structures 
    • Nonlinear Energy Transfers and Harvesting 
    • Vibration and Stability of Systems 
    • Computational Methods 
    • Optimization and Control 
    • Sensitivity Analysis and Design
    • Nonlinear Dynamics and Fracture of Composite Structures
    • Nonlinear Metamaterials and Metastructures
    • Soft Systems and Structures
    • Nonlinear Noisy Systems

Topic Name: MSNDC-03 Contact Dynamics of Mechanical Structures
Topic Description: This symposium is focused on the study of mechanical joints, contact, friction, and damping.  The aim is to promote discussion, enhance understanding, and generate new insights into the connections between tribological-level friction, contact mechanics, and the dynamic responses of built-up assemblies with mechanical contact at a structural level. This symposium invites papers addressing all aspects of the dynamics and mechanics of contact and friction, with particular emphasis on the following challenges: reduced order modeling, advanced analytical/numerical methods, nonlinear analysis, nonlinear normal modes, data-driven methods, and reverse modeling and system identification. Other key areas of interest include hysteresis in jointed structures, the repeatability and variability of response, physical theories and studies of friction, measurements and predictions of energy dissipation and damping, methods to account for uncertainty and nonlinearity in structures with contact and friction, and the development and validation of predictive models of contact.

Topic Name: MSNDC-04 Data-Driven and Machine Learning Techniques in Vibrations and Dynamics
MSNDC-05/VIB-05:  Joint Session Industry Applications of Vibration, Shock, Acoustics, and Dynamics
Topic Description: The symposium on Industrial Applications of Vibration, Shock, Acoustics, and Dynamics provides a forum for sharing ideas, activities, best practices, and innovative solutions to applied problems faced by industry, national laboratories, academia, and related partners. Applications ranging from the automotive industry to national defense increasingly require innovative analysis, simulation and testing to solve complex problems involving vibration, acoustics, and dynamics phenomena. Abstracts are invited that cover standard and nonstandard, multi-disciplinary, and systems-level techniques in vibration, acoustics, dynamics, and related areas of application.

Topic Name: MSNDC-06 Dynamics of Biological, Bio-Inspired and Biomimetic Systems
Topic Description: This symposium brings together a diverse set of researchers who are at the forefront of the emerging field of studying the dynamic aspects of Biological, Bio-inspired and Biomimetic Systems. Researchers conducting traditional or non-traditional academic research, or those driven by industrial applications present their experimental, analytical, and computational studies with Biological, Bio-Inspired and Biomimetic Systems at their focus.

Topic Name: MSNDC-07 Computational Methods and Software Tools in Multibody Systems and Nonlinear Dynamics
Topic Description:
The symposium focuses on recent advances in theoretical, computational, and applied aspects related to the synthesis, simulation, analysis, control, and optimization of multibody systems and nonlinear dynamics. The scope of the symposium encompasses theoretical developments and novel algorithms, implementation techniques, experimentation and validation, and practical applications. 

Submissions are welcome on the following and related topics: efficient algorithms and computational strategies (including real-time simulation, Human/Hardware-in-the-Loop and System-in-the-Loop applications, reduced-order models and surrogate models); co-simulation problems (such as fluid/structure interaction and cyber-physical systems); sensitivity analysis and optimization strategies; uncertainty quantification, simulation and optimization under uncertainty; design of experiments and verification methods; and optimal design and control.

Topic Name: MSNDC-08 Motion Planning, Dynamics, and Control of Robots
Topic Description:
Papers are solicited in the areas of motion planning, dynamics, and control of robots and mechanisms. Theoretical, experimental, and computational aspects are all invited. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:
•	Legged and mobile robots
•	Serial and parallel robots
•	Cable robot and tensegrity mechanism
•	Dynamic analysis, modeling, and simulation
•	Control methods and controller design
•	Trajectory optimization and optimal control
•	Applications of machine learning and AI
•	Manipulation and locomotion planning
•	Stability and efficiency
•	Mission planning, path planning, and motion planning for robots and autonomous systems

Topic Name: MSNDC-09 Advances in Vehicle Dynamics and Control
Topic Description: This symposium highlights recent developments in multibody modeling of vehicle dynamics, including control, stability and multi-physics domain computation. Submissions are welcome in the fields of tire/terrain and wheel/rail interactions, vehicle control, including autonomous mobility, intelligent transportation systems, ride comfort, vehicle subsystem modeling, next-generation simulation tools, validation and verification. The symposium aims to provide a platform to discuss the latest research developments, while also welcoming presentations on cutting-edge industrial applications in vehicle modeling for advanced design, the development of digital twins, and advanced control systems.

Topic Name: MSNDC-10 Flexible Multibody Dynamics
Topic Description: The symposium invites submissions on finite element methods in dynamics and formulations for flexible multibody systems, such as the floating frame of reference and absolute nodal coordinate formulation, including approaches for model order reduction. We are interested in contributions addressing the dynamics of solids and slender structures undergoing large deformations, as well as related topics. Additionally, we welcome research in flexible multibody dynamics covering computational methods, analytical or data-driven approaches, experimental techniques, and applications, e.g., in industrial or biomechanical contexts.

Topic Name: MSNDC-11/VIB-06: Joint Session Design for Blue Economy
Topic Description:
With this session, the ASME Design Automation Technical Committee and TC of Vibration and Sounds invite researchers to submit papers that focus on advancing design methods and systems science to address the emerging challenges and opportunities of the Blue Economy. The Blue Economy encompasses the sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth, improved livelihoods, and ecosystem health, spanning domains such as marine renewable energy, aquaculture, marine transport, ocean monitoring, and coastal resilience. As global pressures on marine environments increase, design automation and systems approaches will play a crucial role in developing innovative, scalable, and resilient solutions.
We welcome contributions that present new design representations, modeling approaches, dynamics, solution methods, and frameworks that extend the frontier of how engineering design can support sustainable ocean-based industries. Submissions may also highlight interdisciplinary integration, where engineering methods connect with ecological, social, and policy considerations. Approaches that enable optimization, control, uncertainty management, and lifecycle thinking for marine-related systems are particularly encouraged. Papers should demonstrate relevance through case studies, benchmarks, or comparative analyses that highlight how design automation and dynamics can directly contribute to advancing Blue Economy goals.
Suggested topic areas covered under this session include:
•	Design methodologies, dynamic modelling, prototypes, and testing for offshore renewable energy systems (wave, tidal, floating wind)
•	Sustainable aquaculture systems and marine food production design
•	Ocean-based carbon capture, sequestration, and monitoring systems
•	Autonomous marine vehicles and robotics for exploration, monitoring, and operations
•	Multi-objective design under uncertainty for coupled ocean–human systems
•	Circular economy strategies for marine materials, products, and infrastructure
•	Resilient coastal and port infrastructure design for the Blue Economy and climate adaptation
•	Computational tools and frameworks for marine ecosystem services integration
•	Systems-level analysis and optimization for ocean resource allocation and governance

Topic Name: PTG 01: Bearings, Clutches, Couplings, and Splines
Topic Description: Design, performance, and integration of key transmission components.

Topic Name: PTG-02: Gear Analysis, Materials, and Fatigue
Topic Description: Analytical and computational methods, material performance, and fatigue life prediction.

Topic Name: PTG-03:  Gear Dynamics and Noise
Topic Description: Modeling and control of vibration, transmission error, and noise reduction.

Topic Name: PTG-04:  Gear Geometry
Topic Description: Advances in macro- and micro-geometry design, optimization, and novel tooth forms.

Topic Name: PTG-05:  Gear Manufacturing
Topic Description: Innovations in hobbing, grinding, additive manufacturing, and process optimization.

Topic Name: PTG-06:  Gearbox Design, Reliability, and Diagnostics
Topic Description: Concepts for robust gearbox design, health monitoring, and fault detection.

Topic Name: PTG-07:  Transmission Systems Including Novel Concepts
Topic Description: Emerging architectures, hybrid/electric drives, and unconventional power transmission solutions.

Topic Name: PTG-08: Lubrication and Efficiency
Topic Description: Tribology, lubricant formulations, and methods to improve power loss and thermal behavior.

Topic Name: VIB-07: Dynamics & Waves in Solids, Acoustic Metamaterials, and Architected Materials
Topic Description: This symposium solicits papers in the broad area of dynamic phenomena of a wave-like nature in solids and metamaterials. Submissions are invited, but not limited to, papers addressing phononic crystals, acoustic metamaterials, metasurfaces, topological insulators, ultrasonics, nonlinear wave propagation, and wave-based devices. This can include studies of negative refractive index, acoustic cloaking, non-reciprocal wave transport, flat modes, topological edge states, quantum analogs, nonlinear behavior, and novel applications of acoustic materials aimed at solving contemporary problems. Other topics that may be of interest include novel fabrication and manufacturing technologies (e.g., self-assembly, additive manufacturing) which enable applications, new computational approaches for simulating wave propagation, and advances in experimental measurements of wave propagation in mechanical systems.

Topic Name: VIB-08: Energy Harvesting
Topic Description:
This symposium invites contributions that push the boundaries of innovation in capturing and converting ambient energy. The scope is vibrational energy harvesting from diverse sources including, but not limited to, mechanical vibrations, nonlinear dynamic behaviors, flow-induced vibrations, ocean waves, acoustic waves, aerodynamic instabilities, and other fluid-structure interactions.
This symposium welcomes contributions that utilize analytical models, numerical simulations, or experimental breakthroughs. Topics of interest include advancements in energy circuits, cutting-edge storage technologies, and the potential of smart materials, metamaterials, and electromechanical transducers. Contributions exploring energy harvesting from these materials, as well as innovations in energy conversion mechanisms, power management circuits, and wearable technologies, are highly encouraged. This symposium seeks novel applications and solutions that have the potential to redefine the future of sustainable energy.

Topic Name: VIB-09: Vibration Measurement, Signal Processing, and Structural Damage Detection
Topic Description: This symposium focuses on, but is not limited to, vibration measurements using traditional methods and nontraditional methods such as laser vibrometry and high-speed digital image correlation; modal testing; signal processing; finite element modeling; model updating; and structural damage detection using vibration-, wave-, and acoustics-based methods.

Topic Name: VIB-10: General Dynamics, Vibration, and Acoustics
Topic Description:
We invite papers on all aspects of dynamics, vibration, and acoustics. Contributions may be theoretical, computational, or experimental, and may address linear or nonlinear phenomena. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:
•	Modal analysis and experimental system identification
•	Advanced computational methods and algorithms
•	Energy-based (Lagrangian/Hamiltonian) and related variational approaches, including non-Hamiltonian systems
•	Dynamics of conservative and non-conservative systems
•	Vibration control, isolation, and mitigation strategies
•	Cross-disciplinary and emerging applications
•	Gear vibration and rotating machinery
•	Topological acoustics (geometric phases, synthetic pseudospin) with applications in information encoding, RF devices, sensing, imaging, and beyond.
•	Dynamics of Biological, Bio-Inspired and Biomimetic Systems
We welcome submissions that push the boundaries of theory, modeling, and practical applications.
